method: Live AAFDID pages were read through a fetch tool and compared row by row with the August 2026 capture. All 80 MCA milestone rows and every row of the other MCA, MTA, SWA, UCA and DBS tables were located live. The corrections below are the only differences found.

corrections.evidence: Live Program Type cell reads 'ACAT IC OR ID (MDAP)ACAT IAM OR IAC (MAIS)ACAT II (Major Systems)ACAT III and below' (?search=PLAN).
Live Program Type cell lists ACAT IAM OR IAC (MAIS) (?search=SYSTEM).

corrections.note: The capture embedded footnote digits in the action text and cut action 6. Clean text and footnotes below were confirmed on the live page.

rows.action: Determine that the acquisition supports core, priority functions of the DoD.
Establish outcome-based performance measures linked to strategic goals.
rows.documentation: ICD, IS ICD, CDD, AoA, APB

rows.action: Redesign the processes that the system supports to reduce costs, improve effectiveness and maximize the use of commercial off-the-shelf technology.
Determine that no private sector or government source can better support the function.
Conduct an economic analysis that includes a calculation of the return on investment; or for non-AIS programs, conduct a life-cycle cost estimate.
Develop clearly established measures and accountability for program progress.
Ensure that the acquisition is consistent with the DoD Information Enterprise policies and architecture, as described in DoDI 5000.82.
Ensure that the program has a Cybersecurity Strategy that is consistent with DoD policies, standards and architectures, to include relevant standards.

Ensure, to the maximum extent practicable, (1) modular contracting has been used, and (2) the program is being implemented in phased, successive increments, each of which meets part of the mission need and delivers measurable benefit, independent of future increments.
Register Mission-Critical and Mission-Essential systems with the DoD CIO.

footnote_text.1: The Milestone and Phase Information Requirements table indicates when the PM must report CCA compliance.
footnote_text.2: The system documents and information cited are examples of the most likely, but not the only, references for the required information.
footnote_text.3: These requirements are presumed to be satisfied for weapons systems with embedded IT and for command and control systems that are not themselves IT systems.
footnote_text.4: These actions are also required to comply with section 811 of Pub. L. 106-398.
footnote_text.5: For national security systems, these requirements apply to the extent practicable (40 U.S.C. 11103).
footnote_text.6: Mission-critical and mission-essential information system definitions are on the source page.
footnote_text.7: The APB and TEMP may be submitted in draft to expedite program assessment.

rows.name: Acquisition Strategy, to include security, schedule, technical, and production risks; a test strategy or an assessment of test results with validation of required cybersecurity and interoperability as applicable; and a transition plan

footnote_text.1: Non-major: equal to or below the threshold in 10 U.S.C. 3041(c) and 4202(b) (formerly 2302d).
footnote_text.2: Major: above the threshold in 10 U.S.C. 3041(c) and 4202(b) (formerly 2302d).
footnote_text.3: Exceeds MDAP threshold: as defined in 10 U.S.C. 4201 and 4202 (formerly 2430).
footnote_text.4: For initial submission, a test strategy can be used in lieu of an assessment of test results if testing is not complete. Programs on the DOT&E oversight list may need additional documentation.
footnote_text.5: Per DoDI 5000.73, CAPE estimates life-cycle costs for Rapid Prototyping programs likely to exceed the ACAT I threshold, and for Rapid Fielding programs likely to exceed the ACAT I or II thresholds.
